arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Carter Phillips argued the Federal Arbitration Act makes arbitration a matter of consent.
Phillips claimed the South Carolina Supreme Court violated this core federal principle.
Ms. Pillard stated Green Tree initially asked the arbitrator to decide on class status.
Pillard argued parties can include clauses prohibiting class arbitration if they wish.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The dispute centers on whether the Federal Arbitration Act preempts state court rules that allow class arbitration. Green Tree Financial argues the federal law mandates individual arbitration. Bazzle contends state law supports the class proceeding.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Green Tree Financial wants the Court to reverse the state court decision and enforce the individual arbitration clause.
Bazzle wants the Court to affirm the state court decision and allow the class arbitration to continue.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case determines whether federal law forces individual arbitration or allows state courts to permit class claims. The outcome shapes how consumers and companies resolve disputes under arbitration agreements nationwide.
